name: Ursodeoxycholic Acid
sections: White crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water; melting point 203 °C.
Originally identified in bear bile (hence 'urso'); first-line therapy for primary biliary cholangitis. First approval/introduction: Chemically synthesised in Japan 1955; US approval 1987.

Replaces toxic hydrophobic bile acids, reduces cholesterol saturation of bile (enabling dissolution of cholesterol gallstones), protects cholangiocytes and hepatocytes (anti-apoptotic, immunomodulatory) and stimulates bile flow. Receptor / target profile: Replaces hydrophobic bile acids, reduces biliary cholesterol saturation, stimulates bile flow, and has cytoprotective, anti-apoptotic and immunomodulatory effects.
Hepatic conjugation with glycine/taurine; enterohepatic circulation; bacterial 7-dehydroxylation to lithocholic acid
Summary: Absorbed in small intestine; extensive first-pass hepatic extraction and conjugation; enterohepatic circulation; excreted in faeces.
Dissolution of radiolucent cholesterol gallstones in a functioning gallbladder
Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, cholestatic liver disease, intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (specialist use)
Prevention of gallstones during rapid weight loss
PBC: 13–15 mg/kg/day in 2–4 divided doses with food
Gallstone dissolution: 8–12 mg/kg/day (single bedtime dose or divided) for 6–24 months
Gallstone prevention in rapid weight loss: 300 mg twice daily
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Main indication; caution in decompensated cirrhosis.
Avoid in first trimester; used in intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy under specialist care.
Calcified, radio-opaque or bile-pigment gallstones; non-functioning gallbladder
Monitor LFTs regularly in liver disease
Gallstone dissolution requires functioning gallbladder and radiolucent stones ≤15 mm
Cholestyramine, colestipol and Al-containing antacids bind UDCA – separate by 2 h
Oestrogens and clofibrate increase biliary cholesterol (counteract effect)
Take with meals; avoid antacids containing aluminium within 2 hours.
LFTs every 4 weeks for 3 months then every 3 months; gallbladder ultrasound at 6–10 months for stone dissolution.
Poupon et al., NEJM 1994 and combined analyses (Lindor 1996) – UDCA improved biochemistry and transplant-free survival in PBC.
Effective for dissolution of small radiolucent cholesterol gallstones.
Stone dissolution needs months of therapy
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
